Check consistency of background probabilities and excitation weights

Source: R/sampling_branching.r
check_branching_weights.Rd

For each event i, verifies that bgprobs[i] + sum(pair_weights[pairs$i == i]) equals 1 (up to a numerical tolerance) – the condition sample_branching() relies on for u ~ Uniform(0, 1) to be partitioned correctly between the background outcome and every candidate-parent outcome. Call this once before drawing samples with sample_branching()/sample_branching_multi().

Usage

check_branching_weights(bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights

Same as in sample_branching().

tol

Numerical tolerance for the sum-to-1 check; default 1e-6.

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_branching_check" with elements:

totals

Numeric vector, one entry per event: bgprobs[i] + sum(pair_weights[pairs$i == i]).

max_abs_error

max(abs(totals - 1)).

n_no_parents

Number of events with bgprobs[i] < 1 but no row in pairs (candidate parents) – these silently fall back to background in sample_branching(), which is only correct if bgprobs[i] is actually 1 for those events.

ok

TRUE if max_abs_error <= tol and n_no_parents == 0.

Examples

bgprobs <- c(1, 0.4, 0.5, 0.2)
pairs <- data.frame(i = as.integer(c(2, 3, 3, 4, 4)),
                    j = as.integer(c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3)))
pair_weights <- c(0.6, 0.3, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3)

check <- check_branching_weights(bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights)
check
#> <semihawkes_branching_check>
#>   max |total - 1| = 0
#>   events with no candidate parents (bgprobs < 1): 0
#>   ok: TRUE
stopifnot(check$ok)
